# Independent audit: near-triangle quadrilateral cap stability

Source: near-triangle-quadrilateral-linear-cap-stability-and-outer-extraction.md.

verifier review/rerun. No source correction was needed.

The standard-library verifier is
verify_near_triangle_quadrilateral_cap_stability.py. It checks 28
quadrilaterals with 224 rational through-point directions each, all
displayed coefficient constants, the exact polygon differences, and
the affine metric bounds. These checks supplement the all-direction
proof, which is audited below.

## Outer triangle and the actual removed region

For p=(1+h-k,k), the side joining p to e_2 meets the x-axis at
b e_1 with b=(1+h-k)/(1-k). The proposed S contains Q and the
line e_1p removes exactly its b e_1 corner. The two incident-edge
fractions are r_1=(b-1)/b=h/(1+h-k) and r_2=k, so the relative
removed area is their product tau. Swapping e_1 and e_2 ensures
k<0.51 and r_1<0.01 throughout the stated h range. This remains
valid when the long cut fraction stays near 1/2; the proof does
not assume both corner fractions tend to zero.

The removed triangle is one actual halfspace trace of S, modulo
its area-zero boundary. Therefore the normalized cap distance
from Q to S equals the nested-body total variation tau, exactly.

## Exhaustion of low-volume cap directions

For a two-vertex cap, complementary edge parameters give area
at most max(lambda_j/(1-lambda_k),lambda_k/(1-lambda_j))<=17/33
for the complementary vertex cap. Hence the original cap has
fraction at least 16/33>4/9+1/10000. Through an interior candidate
there cannot be a zero-vertex or a nontrivial whole-triangle cap
that invalidates this classification. Vertex-boundary directions
are handled by the same limiting area bounds.

For a proper one-vertex cap, the through-point equation and
lambda_j>=9997/30000 give the exact sum bound 30000/9997. The
low-area condition gives product at least 90000/40009. The two
displayed strict rational product gaps then force BOTH cap
coefficients into (29/20,31/20). The product comparison uses the
correct increasing/decreasing sides of x(U-x); neither coefficient
is treated independently of the through-point equation.

## Coupled losses and the candidate's actual depth

On the removed corner, u=lambda_1<=r_1<1/100. A vertex-1 cap
has left side at least (29/20)(1-u)>1, and therefore loses zero
area. A vertex-2 cap requires
v>=1-1/a_0+(a_1/a_0-1)u>=9/29-1/1550>3/10.
The removed triangle's area above v=3/10 is at most
(1-(3/10)/(51/100))^2=49/289<1/5. Thus its loss is at most
tau/5. The vertex-0 loss is bounded by the whole tau. All three
bounds hold for the SAME relevant cap, not separate idealized cuts.

The candidate in the note is interior to Q because its positive
lambda_1 is larger than r_1. Its barycentrics lie in the window
needed for the normal classification. Multiplying their pairs
and subtracting (tau,0,tau/5) gives the three exact polynomials
printed in the source. The worst is Gamma-2tau/5-27tau^2/50.
Higher-volume caps lose at most tau<=kappa and remain above
Gamma, so the argument covers every halfspace direction. After
normalization, subtraction of tau/45 has numerator
tau(10-233tau)/450 over denominator 1-tau, which is positive in
the entire stated range. This proves the actual-center bound,
not only a bound on three canonical cap values.

## The metric normalization does not assume an optimal triangle

The selected Q vertices maximizing x_1, maximizing x_2 and
minimizing x_1+x_2 are within 3delta in infinity norm of e_1,e_2,0.
They are distinct. The two edge vectors are within 6delta of
the standard basis, hence their determinant is at least
(1-6delta)^2-(6delta)^2=1-12delta. The containing coordinate
triangle has area (1+4delta)^2/2. This gives the stated ratio
h<=(20delta+16delta^2)/(1-12delta)<=24delta<=1/10000.

For a strict four-vertex convex polygon, the omitted vertex lies
outside precisely the triangle's diagonal edge and inside its
other two supporting halfplanes. After relabeling, its normalized
coordinates are positive and sum to 1+h. Thus it has exactly
the bump form used earlier. If a putative vertex is collinear
and redundant, the body is already a triangle. Affine maps
preserve both normalized ordinary depth and cap distance.

The comparison triangle is constructed, never optimized. The
result controls its ENTIRE missing area, including the part away
from the removed vertex. It is scoped to this explicit affine
neighborhood of triangles and does not imply the corresponding
statement for arbitrary polygons or changing smooth roofs.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
